sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repository is

`theta-agent` — a **pi package** (extensions + skills for the [pi](https://pi.dev) coding agent) that grows into **Theta**, a science co-researcher agent for biology/biomedicine. It is the code repo of the Theta campaign; design decisions (T1–T10), milestone definitions, and task handoffs live in the campaign vault (path in `CLAUDE.local.md`). Treat the vault as read-only reference.

Current state: 0.5.0 — M5 is shipped. The M1 base ships the `theta` launcher (a thin `bin/theta.mjs` that runs `pi -e <package-root>`; macOS/Linux — Windows waits for M8, tracked in issue #2) and the Tier-1 library: K-Dense skills vendored verbatim per ADR 0001 plus the self-authored `theta-research-loop` orchestrator, with re-syncs at milestone boundaries (`docs/agents/resync.md`). M2 adds the first connector skill, `theta-lit-search` (PubMed, arXiv, Semantic Scholar), landed tracer-first: search and get-by-identifier with pacing, in-200 error detection, and credential redaction enforced in its scripts (ADR 0002; script invariants in `docs/agents/connector-scripts.md`). M3 adds `theta-notebook`, the project notebook skill (ADR 0003): five dated provenance-entry types with content-addressed, graded evidence snapshots under the research project's `.theta/`, a recorder script under the connector-script invariants, a notebook-written attestation in the dogfood auditor, and orchestrator doctrine weaving recording into all six loop stages. M4 ships the compute gateway `theta-compute` (ADR 0004) from `gateway/` — a FastMCP server wrapping the Slurm CLI with argv arrays only, bearer auth from deploy-time env, one audit JSONL line per tool call, and the seven generic tools (the read-only environments/status pair plus the stage–submit–logs–cancel–fetch lifecycle) behind the path sandbox and the command guard, plus the typed `run_alphafold3` rendering the deploy-time template registry's registered template with its free variables only — all out of the npm tarball. On the theta side, M4 landed the gateway skill's lifecycle doctrine and the submit gate (#54), and the notebook's job-record path (#55): a compute run records a method entry whose evidence item is the assembled gateway job record, graded `re-executed` when its artifacts were fetched, and the orchestrator's execute stage routes cluster jobs to `theta-compute`. M5 stacks the safety gates: the deploy-time submit capability (ADR 0006) and the per-principal submit ceiling on the gateway, and on the theta side the submit gate grown into the stacked gate framework (#95) — the literal three-tool confirm set pinned against the gateway's destructive annotations (disagreement is drift and refuses loudly), concurrency-safe stacked confirms (pi 1.4.0's concurrent-dialog fix is the floor), `parentToolCallId` riding prompts, refusals, and the session-dir gate log (`gate.jsonl`, one JSONL line per gated decision), and the dogfood auditor reading codemode's `nestedCalls` records instead of assuming a flat call sequence. M5 S3 (#96) makes the rig itself gateway-bearing: the clean-room rig admits the gateway token as its second credential (`--gateway`, URL host rewritten to the Docker host alias, preflighted in-container before launch — the token rides a 0600 env file, never argv), a checked-in RPC confirm driver (`test/rig/rpc-driver.mjs`) answers the submit gate for headless `--rpc` evidence legs, the gateway skill carries the capability/throttle/codemode doctrine, the auditor finds the transcript by its own name grammar beside the gate log, and the M5 dogfood (gated submit with confirm, held refusal, throttle) ran in the rig against the live gateway. M6 opens the eval suite (ADR 0007) with the replay net's tracer (#133): a checked-in scenario list (`test/eval/scenarios.mjs`), the typed normalization layer with its five rewrite classes, and one connector fixture — a sanitized rig capture — pinned three ways in the keyless standard suite (provenance: one digest per model-visible surface class, so a model-visible edit reds until a fresh capture; snapshot: the normalized entry tree equals its committed snapshot; determinism: pi's reconstruction yields one context hash), with the capture pipeline (`test/eval/capture.mjs`) and doctrine in `docs/agents/eval.md` — all outside the npm tarball. M6 S1 (#134) extends the net to one fixture per model-visible surface class — orchestrator doctrine, the notebook recorder, the gateway skill, and the extension's user-facing strings (the submit gate's refusal, captured on a `--gateway` rig leg where print mode refuses the submit before any server call) — each with its scenario, sanitized fixture, and the three pins; the per-scenario shape assertion lives in `test/eval/shape.mjs`, and the orchestrator fixture binds the vendored skill its doctrine routes to, so a body-only re-sync reds by name. M6 S2 (#135) lands the benchmark layer's tracer beside the net: the rig runner's eval mode runs one checked-in benchmark task end-to-end from one command carrying only the provider key (it refuses `--gateway`/`--rpc` — no gateway token path exists on a benchmark leg), grades workspace-as-oracle through declarative checks run in-container plus one `models.classify()` judge whose named slot runs host-side so its key never enters the rig, and writes the report — task grade, judge tier, UsageEntry totals — beside the recorded exit status.

## pi-package rules

- Host-provided packages (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`, `@earendil-works/pi-tui`, `typebox`) go in `peerDependencies` with `"*"` ranges — never `dependencies`, never bundled.
- Keep the `pi-package` keyword (gallery eligibility) and the explicit `pi` manifest (`extensions`, `skills`) in `package.json`. Manifest fields are arrays of strings — pi silently drops bare-string fields (guarded by `test/manifest.test.mjs`).
- Never install `pi-mcp-adapter` — an installed adapter replaces pi's built-in MCP support (native since pi 0.99).
- Target pi ≥ 1.4.0 and Node ≥ 22.19.0. The floor moves only at milestone boundaries, under the standing adoption rule recorded on #87 — a held review is recorded on the parent spec, never silent. Package loading uses `pi -e <source>`; local-path sources load without copying, so a repo checkout works exactly like the installed package.
- The pi extension API is read from the installed package, not the web — the paths below sit under the pi install root (`$(npm root -g)/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/`): `docs/extensions.md` (events, the tool-call pipeline, UI modes), `docs/mcp.md` (tool naming and exposure — MCP tool names are sanitized to `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, so a server hyphen registers as an underscore), and `dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts` for the exact event and context shapes.

## Conventions

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `chore:`, `docs:`). Tabs and existing field order in `package.json`.
- Extract a shared helper as soon as the same logic shape appears twice — tree-wide, not per-module: a module boundary created mid-strike is where duplication is born, so the shared shape gets one home before the second caller (tests included). Copying code verbatim is for separately shipped trees only — skill-to-skill, never within a file.
- Failure paths in runner and helper scripts: child-process spawns inherit the environment (overlay onto `process.env`, never replace it — the eslint `spawn-env-inherit` rule enforces direct call sites); `finally` cleanup never masks the primary failure; a machine-readable result lands as a file when its channel is shared with payload output (the exit-status rule — and a pipeline whose exit gates the next step runs unpiped or under `set -o pipefail`: a `tee` or `tail` in the tail position reports its own status, and #117's failed cluster re-deploy sailed through an `&&` chain that way).
- An accepted behavior delta — ordering, precedence, message bytes — is pinned by a test in the same strike; the PR body discloses what the suite already owns (#113's read-precedence delta reached the merge round disclosed but unpinned, and the merge round paid the pin).
- The review round names every accepted deviation from the spec's letter — additions beyond the enumeration included — with the reason; the disclosure lands in the same strike's PR body, not in a later pass (#127's survey-inputs bullet rode through PR #128's draft review undisclosed, and the triage round paid the disclosure).
- An extraction test — one that pulls structured tokens out of prose — consumes from its anchor: the match opens the claim it pins, leading whitespace only, never searching forward past other text. An unanchored match can borrow a later passage and pass silently (#122's review round caught the prose check's enumeration doing exactly that).

2. The reverse order pays a full recapture every time a review fix moves HEAD — M5 S3 and S4 each paid one on 2026-10-31 (three live legs with cluster toggles; the closeout pair), review-first would have paid neither. # Theta project notebook

The third Theta-owned skill: the recorder for the **project notebook** (ADR
0003) — the durable record of a research effort, accumulating across
sessions and tools in the research project's workspace. A session transcript
dies with the session; the notebook belongs to the project.

## Where the notebook lives

Plain files under `.theta/` in the workspace the session runs in:

- `notebook.jsonl` — one JSON entry per line, **append-only**. Inspect, diff,
  back up, version — no pi runtime needed.
- `evidence/` — sha256-addressed snapshots, one file per evidence item. Same
  bytes, same name: identical evidence stored twice is one file.

## The five entry types

One recorder call appends one entry. Every entry carries its `id` (sequenced
per type), its `type`, the `date` it was recorded, and its `text`.

| Type | Ids | Text flag | Evidence | Also carries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hypothesis | `hyp-0001`… | `--hypothesis` | required | — |
| method | `mth-0001`… | `--method` | optional | — |
| observation | `obs-0001`… | `--observation` | required | its own `grade`; items may link |
| decision | `dec-0001`… | `--decision` | optional | — |
| confidence | `cnf-0001`… | `--confidence` | never | the `hypothesis` it judges (`--on`) |

- A hypothesis or an observation is a claim about what a source showed, so
  evidence is required. A method or a decision may stand on the researcher's
  reasoning; record the motivating search as its evidence when one exists.
- A confidence entry is judgment, not a source claim: it takes no evidence,
  and `--on` names the hypothesis entry it judges — recorded later, so the
  judgment history sits next to the evidence it weighs.
- **Evidence-to-hypothesis links**: an observation's evidence item may carry
  `supports: hyp-0001` (`--supports`), marking it as backing an existing
  hypothesis. The recorder refuses a link that names no recorded hypothesis.
  A hypothesis entry's own evidence needs no link — it backs that entry.

A hypothesis entry, and an observation linked to it, from the same notebook:

```json
{
  "id": "hyp-0001",
  "type": "hypothesis",
  "date": "2026-10-19",
  "text": "CRISPR-based gene editing can restore immune cell function in aged organisms",
  "evidence": [
    {
      "source": "pubmed",
      "endpoints": ["esearch.fcgi", "esummary.fcgi"],
      "query": "CRISPR gene therapy",
      "retrieved": "2026-10-18",
      "grade": "asserted",
      "snapshot": "evidence/<sha256>.json"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "obs-0001",
  "type": "observation",
  "date": "2026-10-20",
  "text": "Two independent retrievals agree that HDR-mediated repair is rare in HSCs",
  "grade": "cross-checked",
  "evidence": [
    {
      "source": "pubmed",
      "endpoints": ["esearch.fcgi", "esummary.fcgi"],
      "query": "CRISPR gene therapy",
      "retrieved": "2026-10-18",
      "grade": "cross-checked",
      "snapshot": "evidence/<sha256>.json",
      "supports": "hyp-0001"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `date` is the day the entry was recorded; `retrieved` is the day the
  connector made its call (the connector's `provenance.accessed`, carried
  through). Two different claims, both kept.
- The evidence item carries the source, the endpoints called, the query, the
  retrieval date, the grade, and the snapshot address. `query` is the search
  term, or null for an identifier lookup (whose identifiers ride in the
  snapshot itself).
- A **job record** (ADR 0004) is the evidence item of the method entry that
  records a compute run: the gateway as its `source`, the job ID, the
  template (null for a raw submit), the argument digest, the final state,
  and the artifact manifest when the artifacts were fetched. Its `retrieved`
  is the day the record's state was observed. The recorder accepts the grade
  `re-executed` only when the manifest is present.
- The snapshot is the evidence source's structured output byte-for-byte —
  the connector's `--json` output (already credential-redacted and already
  dated by the connector's own code) or the assembled job record. Raw HTTP
  bodies are never kept.

## When to record

- The loop's hypothesize moment: a hypothesis has survived framing and
  search, and the connector output that motivated it is in hand.
- The design moment: a method is chosen or discarded — record the choice,
  with the search that motivated it as evidence when there is one.
- The execute moment: reading a result off a search output is an
  observation; when it backs an existing hypothesis, link the evidence. A
  compute run that closes out records its job record as a method entry —
  the theta-compute doctrine walks the lifecycle.
- Any point a direction is set or cut: a decision, recorded as its own
  entry so the correction of an earlier entry is a later entry, never a
  rewrite of history.
- When judgment moves: a confidence entry on a named hypothesis — raised,
  lowered, or held, with the reasoning in the text.
- A standalone literature search outside the orchestrator loop that lands a
  claim worth keeping — any session that finds evidence leaves its trace.
- Record only through this skill's script. Never edit `notebook.jsonl` by
  hand; the recorder refuses to append to a notebook it cannot parse, and
  append-only is the format's contract.

## Operations

The recorder writes `.theta/` under the **current directory**, so run it with
the research project's workspace as the cwd — never from inside the skill
tree, which would land the notebook in the package checkout. Resolve the
script path against the skill directory (pi's rule for skill-relative paths)
and pass it absolute:

```bash
cd /path/to/research-project

# The real flow — a hypothesis off a live search, piped straight in:
python3 <theta-lit-search-skill-dir>/scripts/pubmed.py --query "CRISPR gene therapy" --json | \
  python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --hypothesis "TEXT" --evidence - --grade asserted

# The chosen method, with the search that motivated it:
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --method "TEXT" --evidence search.json --grade asserted

# An observation, its evidence linked to the hypothesis it supports:
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --observation "TEXT" --evidence search.json --grade cross-checked --supports hyp-0001

# A decision (no evidence needed), and a confidence judgment:
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py --decision "TEXT"
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --confidence "TEXT" --on hyp-0001

# A compute run closes out: the assembled job record rides a method entry
# (theta-compute's doctrine assembles it from the gateway answers):
python3 <theta-notebook-skill-dir>/scripts/notebook.py \
  --method "TEXT" --job-record job-record.json --grade re-executed
```

`--evidence` takes the path of a saved `--json` output, or `-` to read it
from stdin; `--job-record` takes an assembled gateway job record the same
way. The two are mutually exclusive — one evidence item per call — and
`--grade` is required exactly when either is given. `--on` and `--supports`
must name a hypothesis entry already in the notebook; a reference that names
no recorded hypothesis is a usage error, never an entry.

Requires Python 3.11+ (standard library only). If `python3` is older, run
`python3.13`, `python3.12`, or `python3.11` — the script names them when the
gate trips. Default output is the recorded line, then the entry's specifics
— the evidence item's source and retrieval date with its grade, and the
snapshot address; `--json` prints the appended entry itself instead.

### The job record's shape

The session assembles the record from the theta-compute answers for one run
and passes it to `--job-record` as JSON (path or `-`):

```json
{
  "gateway": "theta-compute",
  "job_id": "12347",
  "run_name": "af3-lysozyme",
  "template": "alphafold3",
  "arguments_digest": "<sha256 of the job's canonical input>",
  "state": "COMPLETED",
  "observed": "2026-10-25",
  "artifacts": {"run_name": "af3-lysozyme", "total_bytes": 49414,
                "files": [{"path": "alphafold3_output/model.cif", "size": 48211}]}
}
```

- Required: `gateway`, `job_id` (digits), `run_name`, `template` (null for a
  raw submit), `arguments_digest` (a 64-hex sha256), `state`, `observed` —
  the day the state was read, carried through as the item's `retrieved`.
  `artifacts` is present exactly when `fetch_artifacts` answered, and holds
  paths and sizes, never file contents: the recorder refuses a manifest
  that carries `content_b64`. Extra keys (directives, script path) ride in
  the snapshot.
- The evidence item carries the job's fields, the grade, and the snapshot
  address; the snapshot is the assembled record byte-for-byte.
- `re-executed` claims the machinery recomputed the result, so it is honest
  only once the artifacts were fetched — the recorder refuses it without
  the manifest. Until then, `asserted`. Those are the record's two grades:
  `cross-checked` is a retrieval's mark, and the recorder refuses it on a
  job record.

## Grades

The grade marks how much the evidence can be trusted. It grades the source,
never the researcher's judgment — judgment is the confidence entry type, and
the two never merge: an entry that carries a grade is an observation (or an
evidence item inside any entry), and a confidence entry never carries one.

- `asserted` — a single retrieval, not independently verified. The honest
  grade for one literature snapshot; use it unless another genuinely applies.
- `cross-checked` — two independent retrievals were actually compared and
  agree (say, the same record from PubMed and from Semantic Scholar).
- `re-executed` — machinery recomputed the result: a gateway job whose
  artifacts were fetched. The recorder refuses it for a job record without
  the artifact manifest, and a session cannot honestly claim it for a
  literature snapshot.

`--grade` is required exactly when evidence is recorded — never defaulted,
never given without evidence: the trust mark on a source is a decision,
never an accident. On an observation the same flag also grades the entry
itself.

## Exit codes

The exit code is the contract — branch on it, never on the presence of
output. Codes 0 and 1 are the connector scripts' shared meanings; 2 is this
recorder's own failure domain (it makes no requests, so there is no
transport to fail):

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success — the entry is appended and named on stdout. |
| 1 | Usage error — bad arguments, evidence input that is not a valid connector output or gateway job record, or a link naming no recorded hypothesis. |
| 2 | Notebook failure — the notebook cannot be read (corrupt, or `.theta` is not a directory) or written. |

## Output discipline

- Relay the entry id, the grade, and the snapshot address — the researcher
  can find all of it under `.theta/`.
- A failed append is never silently skipped: a non-zero exit reaches the
  user as a failure.
- The snapshot must be the evidence source's final structured output — not a
  hand-composed file, not a raw HTTP body the connector never emitted, not a
  job record padded with file payloads.
- If an entry turns out wrong, the correction is a later decision entry,
  never a rewrite of history.

## Boundaries

- The recorder consumes connector output and assembled job records; it
  never calls a source or a gateway itself, and the theta-lit-search scripts
  are untouched by this skill.
- One evidence item per call; an entry synthesizing several retrievals is
  recorded per source, cross-checked claims included.
- `.theta/` belongs to the research project. In the theta-agent repo's own
  dogfood runs it is gitignored so clean-tree proofs hold; in a research
  project, versioning the notebook is the researcher's choice.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Project notebook recorder: one dated provenance entry per call (ADR 0003).

The notebook lives in the research project's workspace -- a `.theta/`
directory holding `notebook.jsonl` (one JSON entry per line, append-only)
and `evidence/` (sha256-addressed snapshots). Each call records one of the
five entry types -- hypothesis, method, observation, decision, confidence --
with ids sequenced per type so later entries can link to them. An entry that
carries evidence stores the evidence source's structured output verbatim as
its content-addressed snapshot -- a theta-lit-search `--json` output (the
connector's final output: already redacted, already dated; raw HTTP bodies
are never kept) or an assembled theta-compute job record (M4, ADR 0004). A
grade is required exactly when evidence is recorded, and the observation
entry carries it as its own field: a grade rates the source, never the
researcher's judgment -- that judgment is the confidence entry type, and the
two never merge.

Exit codes -- the documented contract (see SKILL.md):
  0  success; the entry is appended and named on stdout
  1  usage error (bad arguments, malformed or shape-invalid evidence input,
     or a link that names no hypothesis in the notebook)
  2  notebook failure (the notebook cannot be read or written)

Usage:
  python3 notebook.py --hypothesis "TEXT" --evidence <connector-output.json|->
      --grade {asserted,cross-checked,re-executed} [--json]
  python3 notebook.py --method "TEXT" [--evidence <...> --grade <...>] [--json]
  python3 notebook.py --observation "TEXT" --evidence <...> --grade <...>
      [--supports hyp-NNNN] [--json]
  python3 notebook.py --decision "TEXT" [--evidence <...> --grade <...>] [--json]
  python3 notebook.py --confidence "TEXT" --on hyp-NNNN [--json]
  python3 notebook.py --method "TEXT" --job-record <job-record.json|->
      --grade {asserted,re-executed} [--json]

`--evidence` is required for hypothesis and observation entries, optional
for method and decision, and rejected for confidence (a judgment is not a
source claim). `--on` and `--supports` must name a hypothesis entry already
in the notebook.

`--job-record` records a compute run: the evidence item is the job record
the session assembles from the theta-compute answers -- job ID, gateway,
run name, template (null for a raw submit), argument digest, final state,
observed date, and the artifact manifest when the artifacts were fetched
(paths and sizes, never file contents). It is mutually exclusive with
`--evidence` -- one evidence item per call -- and shares the pairing rule:
`--grade` is required exactly when either is given, and the record's grades
are `asserted` and `re-executed` (cross-checked is a retrieval's mark). The
grade `re-executed` claims the machinery recomputed the result, so the
recorder accepts it only when the record carries the artifact manifest.

Contract basis: docs/adr/0003-provenance-is-a-project-notebook.md,
docs/adr/0004-compute-is-a-native-mcp-server.md, and the connector-script
invariants (docs/agents/connector-scripts.md).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NoReturn

#: Notebook paths, relative to the research project's workspace (the current
#: directory) -- also the form every message and stdout line names them by.
THETA_DIR = Path(".theta")
NOTEBOOK_PATH = THETA_DIR / "notebook.jsonl"
EVIDENCE_DIR = THETA_DIR / "evidence"

GRADES = ("asserted", "cross-checked", "re-executed")

#: The five entry types (ADR 0003) and the id prefix each sequences under.
TYPE_PREFIX = {
	"hypothesis": "hyp",
	"method": "mth",
	"observation": "obs",
	"decision": "dec",
	"confidence": "cnf",
}

#: A link target or confidence subject: an existing hypothesis entry's id.
REF_RE = re.compile(r"^hyp-\d+$")

#: The connector stamps `provenance.accessed`; the recorder carries it
#: through as the evidence item's retrieval date. `calendar_date` adds the
#: calendar check on top of this shape check.
DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")

#: A job record's identity shapes (ADR 0004): Slurm ids are digits, a run
#: name follows the gateway guard's own rule (1-64 of letters, digits, '-'
#: and '_'), and the argument digest is a sha256 hex string.
JOB_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+$")
RUN_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")
DIGEST_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")

_CONTROL = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]")
_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")


class RecorderError(Exception):
	"""A failure the recorder reported.

	`exit_code` is the script's documented contract code, so callers translate
	an exception directly into a process exit -- no re-classification at the
	top level. (Same idiom as the connector scripts' ApiError.)
	"""

	def __init__(self, message: str, exit_code: int) -> None:
		super().__init__(message)
		self.exit_code = exit_code


# The small helpers from here through fail() are deliberate copies from
# theta-lit-search/scripts/_common.py, not an import: each skill ships as an
# independent tree, so a cross-skill import would couple separately shipped
# code. Keep the copies small.
def require_python() -> None:
	"""Refuse to run below 3.11, naming the versioned fallbacks."""
	if sys.version_info < (3, 11):
		version = ".".join(str(part) for part in sys.version_info[:3])
		fail(
			f"notebook.py: Python 3.11+ required (this interpreter is {version}); "
			"retry with python3.13, python3.12, or python3.11",
			code=1,
		)


def collapse_ws(text: str | None) -> str:
	"""Collapse whitespace runs and drop control characters.

	Same treatment the connectors give API text, applied to the entry text so
	an entry stays one clean line whatever the shell handed in.
	"""
	if not text:
		return ""
	return _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", _CONTROL.sub("", text)).strip()


def calendar_date(text: str) -> bool:
	"""True when a YYYY-MM-DD string names a real calendar date.

	Shape alone is not enough: the dogfood auditor judges retrieval dates
	calendar-valid, and the recorder must refuse what the audit would --
	a written entry cannot be un-written from an append-only file.
	"""
	if not DATE_RE.match(text):
		return False
	try:
		date.fromisoformat(text)
	except ValueError:
		return False
	return True


def emit(payload: object) -> None:
	"""Write `payload` as UTF-8 JSON to stdout."""
	sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


def fail(message: str, code: int) -> NoReturn:
	"""Write `message` to stderr and exit with a contract code."""
	sys.stderr.write(f"{message}\n")
	raise SystemExit(code)


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
	"""argparse exits 2 on usage errors, which the contract reserves for
	notebook failures -- usage errors exit 1 uniformly."""

	def error(self, message: str) -> NoReturn:
		self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
		sys.stderr.write(f"notebook.py: error: {message}\n")
		raise SystemExit(1)


def build_parser() -> Parser:
	parser = Parser(
		prog="notebook.py",
		description="Append one dated provenance entry to the project notebook in "
		".theta/, storing the evidence source's structured output as a "
		"content-addressed evidence item when the entry carries evidence.",
	)
	types = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
	types.add_argument(
		"--hypothesis", help="the hypothesis text to record (evidence required)",
	)
	types.add_argument(
		"--method", help="the chosen method to record (evidence optional)",
	)
	types.add_argument(
		"--observation",
		help="the observation text to record (evidence required; the entry "
		"itself carries the grade)",
	)
	types.add_argument(
		"--decision", help="the decision text to record (evidence optional)",
	)
	types.add_argument(
		"--confidence",
		help="the judgment text on a hypothesis (no evidence: judgment is not "
		"a source claim)",
	)
	parser.add_argument(
		"--on",
		metavar="hyp-NNNN",
		help="the hypothesis entry a confidence entry judges; required with "
		"--confidence, rejected without it",
	)
	parser.add_argument(
		"--evidence",
		help="path to a theta-lit-search --json output, or - to read it from "
		"stdin; required for hypothesis and observation, optional for method "
		"and decision, rejected for confidence",
	)
	parser.add_argument(
		"--job-record",
		metavar="PATH|-",
		help="path to an assembled theta-compute job record (one run's "
		"answers: job ID, gateway, template, argument digest, artifact "
		"manifest, final state), or - to read it from stdin; the evidence "
		"item recording a compute run; mutually exclusive with --evidence",
	)
	parser.add_argument(
		"--grade",
		choices=GRADES,
		help="the evidence grade carried by the recorded evidence item -- and "
		"by the observation entry itself; required exactly when --evidence or "
		"--job-record is given (a trust mark on a source is a decision, never "
		"an accident)",
	)
	parser.add_argument(
		"--supports",
		metavar="hyp-NNNN",
		help="mark the recorded evidence as supporting this existing "
		"hypothesis; observation entries only",
	)
	parser.add_argument(
		"--json", action="store_true", help="print the appended entry as JSON"
	)
	return parser


def read_evidence(spec: str, flag: str = "--evidence") -> str:
	"""The evidence source's structured output text, file or stdin (`-`)."""
	if spec == "-":
		text = sys.stdin.read()
		origin = "stdin"
	else:
		origin = spec
		try:
			text = Path(spec).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
		except OSError as error:
			raise RecorderError(
				f"notebook.py: {flag} unreadable: {origin}: {error}", 1
			) from None
	if not text.strip():
		raise RecorderError(f"notebook.py: {flag} is empty: {origin}", 1)
	return text


def read_payload(text: str, flag: str, what: str) -> dict:
	"""Parse the evidence text as a JSON object, or refuse it as usage."""
	try:
		payload = json.loads(text)
	except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
		raise RecorderError(
			f"notebook.py: {flag} is not valid JSON: {error}", 1
		) from None
	if not isinstance(payload, dict):
		raise RecorderError(
			f"notebook.py: {flag} must be a JSON object -- {what}",
			1,
		)
	return payload


def field_str(container: dict, key: str, message: str) -> str:
	"""One non-empty string field, or a usage refusal naming `message`."""
	value = container.get(key)
	if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
		raise RecorderError(f"notebook.py: {message}", 1)
	return value


def field_date(container: dict, key: str, message: str) -> str:
	"""One calendar-date string field, or a usage refusal naming `message`."""
	value = container.get(key)
	if not isinstance(value, str) or not calendar_date(value):
		raise RecorderError(f"notebook.py: {message}", 1)
	return value


def field_uint(container: dict, key: str, message: str) -> int | None:
	"""One optional non-negative integer field, or a usage refusal.

	A JSON `true`/`false` is not an integer even though Python's bool
	subclasses int -- the manifest's counts refuse it like any other type.
	"""
	value = container.get(key)
	if value is not None and (
		isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0
	):
		raise RecorderError(f"notebook.py: {message}", 1)
	return value


def parse_evidence(text: str) -> dict:
	"""Validate the connector output and extract the evidence item fields.

	Typed shape checks, not presence-only (the connector-script invariant): a
	`provenance.calls` of any other type, or an `accessed` that is not a date
	string, is a malformed input, never a sparse evidence item.
	"""
	payload = read_payload(
		text, "--evidence", "a connector's structured output (--json)"
	)
	source = field_str(
		payload, "source", "--evidence lacks a non-empty string 'source'"
	)
	provenance = payload.get("provenance")
	if not isinstance(provenance, dict):
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --evidence lacks a 'provenance' object", 1
		)
	calls = provenance.get("calls")
	if not isinstance(calls, list) or not calls:
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --evidence provenance.calls must be a non-empty list", 1
		)
	endpoints: list[str] = []
	for call in calls:
		if not isinstance(call, dict):
			raise RecorderError(
				"notebook.py: every provenance call must be an object", 1
			)
		endpoint = field_str(
			call,
			"endpoint",
			"every provenance call needs a non-empty string 'endpoint'",
		)
		field_str(
			call,
			"url",
			"every provenance call needs a non-empty string 'url'",
		)
		if endpoint not in endpoints:
			endpoints.append(endpoint)
	accessed = field_date(
		provenance,
		"accessed",
		"--evidence provenance.accessed must be a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date",
	)
	query = payload.get("query")
	if query is not None and not isinstance(query, str):
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --evidence 'query', when present, must be a string", 1
		)
	return {
		"source": source,
		"endpoints": endpoints,
		"query": query,
		"retrieved": accessed,
	}


def refuse_manifest_contents(where: str) -> NoReturn:
	"""The job record holds the artifact manifest, never the payloads."""
	raise RecorderError(
		f"notebook.py: --job-record artifacts must not carry file contents "
		f"('content_b64' in {where}) -- the record holds paths and sizes; the "
		"bytes stay on the cluster and in the fetched workspace",
		1,
	)


def validate_manifest(artifacts: object, run_name: str) -> dict:
	"""The fetched-artifact manifest of a job record, validated.

	The gateway's fetch answer carries each file's bytes base64-encoded; the
	job record keeps the manifest shape only -- paths and sizes -- so a
	snapshot never re-stores payloads the cluster already holds. The
	manifest's run, when named, must be the record's own run.
	"""
	if not isinstance(artifacts, dict):
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record 'artifacts', when present, must be an object",
			1,
		)
	if "content_b64" in artifacts:
		refuse_manifest_contents("the artifacts object")
	files = artifacts.get("files")
	if not isinstance(files, list) or not files:
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record artifacts.files must be a non-empty list", 1
		)
	for entry in files:
		if not isinstance(entry, dict):
			raise RecorderError(
				"notebook.py: every artifacts.files entry must be an object", 1
			)
		if "content_b64" in entry:
			refuse_manifest_contents("a files entry")
		field_str(
			entry,
			"path",
			"every artifacts.files entry needs a non-empty string 'path'",
		)
		field_uint(
			entry,
			"size",
			"--job-record artifacts file 'size', when present, must be a "
			"non-negative integer",
		)
	field_uint(
		artifacts,
		"total_bytes",
		"--job-record artifacts 'total_bytes', when present, must be a "
		"non-negative integer",
	)
	fetched_run = artifacts.get("run_name")
	if fetched_run is not None and fetched_run != run_name:
		raise RecorderError(
			f"notebook.py: --job-record artifacts.run_name {fetched_run!r} does "
			f"not match the record's run_name {run_name!r}",
			1,
		)
	return artifacts


def parse_job_record(text: str) -> dict:
	"""Validate the assembled gateway job record and extract the item fields.

	The mirror of parse_evidence for the compute path (ADR 0004): the record
	the session assembles from the theta-compute answers must carry the job's
	identity in full -- job ID, gateway, run name, template (null for a raw
	submit), argument digest, final state -- and the day the state was
	observed, which rides through as the item's retrieval date. Typed shape
	checks, not presence-only; the artifact manifest, when fetched, is
	validated by validate_manifest.
	"""
	payload = read_payload(
		text, "--job-record", "an assembled theta-compute job record"
	)
	source = field_str(
		payload, "gateway", "--job-record lacks a non-empty string 'gateway'"
	)
	job_id = payload.get("job_id")
	if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not JOB_ID_RE.match(job_id):
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record 'job_id' must be a string of digits", 1
		)
	run_name = payload.get("run_name")
	if not isinstance(run_name, str) or not RUN_NAME_RE.match(run_name):
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record 'run_name' must be 1-64 characters of "
			"letters, digits, '-' and '_'",
			1,
		)
	if "template" not in payload:
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record must carry 'template' (null for a raw "
			"submit that runs no registered template)",
			1,
		)
	template = payload["template"]
	if template is not None and (not isinstance(template, str) or not template):
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record 'template' must be a non-empty name or "
			"null (a raw submit runs no template)",
			1,
		)
	digest = payload.get("arguments_digest")
	if not isinstance(digest, str) or not DIGEST_RE.match(digest):
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record 'arguments_digest' must be a 64-character "
			"sha256 hex digest",
			1,
		)
	state = payload.get("state")
	# A state copied from a gateway answer is never whitespace-only; unlike
	# entry text it is stored verbatim, so only the emptiness is checked.
	if not isinstance(state, str) or not state.strip():
		raise RecorderError(
			"notebook.py: --job-record lacks a non-empty string 'state'", 1
		)
	item = {
		"source": source,
		"job_id": job_id,
		"template": template,
		"arguments_digest": digest,
		"state": state,
	}
	artifacts = payload.get("artifacts")
	if artifacts is not None:
		item["artifacts"] = validate_manifest(artifacts, run_name)
	item["retrieved"] = field_date(
		payload,
		"observed",
		"--job-record 'observed' must be a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date",
	)
	return item


def load_notebook() -> list[dict]:
	"""Every entry in the existing notebook, parsed.

	The recorder never appends to a notebook it cannot parse: a malformed line
	is a notebook failure, found before anything is written.
	"""
	if not NOTEBOOK_PATH.exists():
		return []
	try:
		raw = NOTEBOOK_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
	except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
		raise RecorderError(
			f"notebook.py: cannot read {NOTEBOOK_PATH}: {error}", 2
		) from None
	entries = []
	for number, line in enumerate(raw.splitlines(), start=1):
		if not line.strip():
			continue
		try:
			entry = json.loads(line)
		except json.JSONDecodeError:
			raise RecorderError(
				f"notebook.py: {NOTEBOOK_PATH} line {number} is not JSON; the "
				"recorder never appends to a notebook it cannot parse",
				2,
			) from None
		if not isinstance(entry, dict):
			raise RecorderError(
				f"notebook.py: {NOTEBOOK_PATH} line {number} is not a JSON object", 2
			)
		entries.append(entry)
	return entries


def next_id(entry_type: str, entries: list[dict]) -> str:
	"""Sequence past the highest existing id of this entry's type."""
	prefix = TYPE_PREFIX[entry_type]
	id_re = re.compile(rf"^{prefix}-(\d+)$")
	highest = 0
	for entry in entries:
		match = id_re.match(str(entry.get("id", "")))
		if match:
			highest = max(highest, int(match.group(1)))
	return f"{prefix}-{highest + 1:04d}"


def resolve_ref(entries: list[dict], ref: str | None, flag: str) -> None:
	"""A --on/--supports reference must name an existing hypothesis entry.

	The id shape is checked at argument-parse time; here the reference must
	resolve against the notebook's hypothesis entries -- a link that points
	nowhere is a usage error, never a recorded entry.
	"""
	if ref is None:
		return
	known = [
		str(entry.get("id"))
		for entry in entries
		if entry.get("type") == "hypothesis"
	]
	if ref not in known:
		raise RecorderError(
			f"notebook.py: {flag} names no hypothesis in the notebook: {ref} "
			f"(hypotheses recorded: {', '.join(known) or 'none'})",
			1,
		)


def write_entry(entry: dict, snapshot: tuple[str, str] | None) -> None:
	"""Store the snapshot, then append the entry; everything after the scan.

	`snapshot` is the evidence's (file name, text) pair, or None for an entry
	that carries no evidence. Order matters: an entry is never appended
	unless its snapshot is already stored, so a crash between the two leaves
	an orphan snapshot, never an entry pointing at nothing.
	"""
	try:
		if snapshot is not None:
			snapshot_name, evidence_text = snapshot
			EVIDENCE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
			snapshot_path = EVIDENCE_DIR / snapshot_name
			if snapshot_path.exists():
				try:
					existing = snapshot_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
				except UnicodeDecodeError:
					existing = None  # undecodable bytes differ from any text
				if existing != evidence_text:
					raise RecorderError(
						f"notebook.py: snapshot collision: {snapshot_name} already "
						"exists with different content",
						2,
					)
			else:
				snapshot_path.write_text(evidence_text, encoding="utf-8")
		with NOTEBOOK_PATH.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
			handle.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
	except OSError as error:
		raise RecorderError(
			f"notebook.py: cannot write the notebook: {error}", 2
		) from None


def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None) -> argparse.Namespace:
	args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
	args.type = next(t for t in TYPE_PREFIX if getattr(args, t) is not None)
	args.text = collapse_ws(getattr(args, args.type))
	if not args.text:
		fail(f"notebook.py: --{args.type} must be non-empty text", 1)
	# Confidence is judgment, not a source claim: no evidence, a named subject.
	if args.type == "confidence":
		if args.evidence is not None or args.job_record is not None:
			fail(
				"notebook.py: --evidence and --job-record are not accepted with "
				"--confidence; a judgment is not a source claim",
				1,
			)
		if args.on is None:
			fail(
				"notebook.py: --confidence requires --on naming the hypothesis "
				"it judges",
				1,
			)
	elif args.on is not None:
		fail("notebook.py: --on is only accepted with --confidence", 1)
	if args.evidence is not None and args.job_record is not None:
		fail(
			"notebook.py: --evidence and --job-record are mutually exclusive -- "
			"one evidence item per call",
			1,
		)
	has_evidence = args.evidence is not None or args.job_record is not None
	if args.type in ("hypothesis", "observation") and not has_evidence:
		fail(
			f"notebook.py: --{args.type} requires --evidence or --job-record -- "
			"a hypothesis or an observation is a claim about what a source "
			"showed",
			1,
		)
	if has_evidence != (args.grade is not None):
		fail(
			"notebook.py: --grade is required exactly when --evidence or "
			"--job-record is given",
			1,
		)
	if args.job_record is not None and args.grade == "cross-checked":
		fail(
			"notebook.py: --grade cross-checked is not accepted with "
			"--job-record; a job record is graded asserted or re-executed",
			1,
		)
	if args.supports is not None and args.type != "observation":
		fail(
			"notebook.py: --supports is only accepted with --observation -- an "
			"evidence-to-hypothesis link rides an observation's evidence",
			1,
		)
	for flag, value in (("--on", args.on), ("--supports", args.supports)):
		if value is not None and not REF_RE.match(value):
			fail(
				f"notebook.py: {flag} must name a hypothesis id (hyp-NNNN), "
				f"got: {value}",
				1,
			)
	return args


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
	require_python()
	args = parse_args(argv)
	if THETA_DIR.exists() and not THETA_DIR.is_dir():
		fail("notebook.py: .theta exists but is not a directory", 2)
	try:
		item = None
		snapshot = None
		evidence_text = ""
		if args.evidence is not None:
			evidence_text = read_evidence(args.evidence)
			item = parse_evidence(evidence_text)
		elif args.job_record is not None:
			evidence_text = read_evidence(args.job_record, "--job-record")
			item = parse_job_record(evidence_text)
			# re-executed claims the machinery recomputed the result; the
			# claim stands on the fetched artifacts the manifest names.
			if args.grade == "re-executed" and item.get("artifacts") is None:
				raise RecorderError(
					"notebook.py: --grade re-executed needs the job record's "
					"artifact manifest -- fetch the artifacts first, or grade "
					"asserted",
					1,
				)
		if item is not None:
			item["grade"] = args.grade
			digest = hashlib.sha256(evidence_text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
			item["snapshot"] = f"evidence/{digest}.json"
			if args.supports is not None:
				item["supports"] = args.supports
			snapshot = (f"{digest}.json", evidence_text)
		entries = load_notebook()
		resolve_ref(entries, args.on, "--on")
		resolve_ref(entries, args.supports, "--supports")
		entry = {
			"id": next_id(args.type, entries),
			"type": args.type,
			"date": date.today().isoformat(),
		}
		if args.type == "confidence":
			entry["hypothesis"] = args.on
		entry["text"] = args.text
		if args.type == "observation":
			entry["grade"] = args.grade
		if item is not None:
			entry["evidence"] = [item]
		write_entry(entry, snapshot)
	except RecorderError as error:
		fail(str(error), error.exit_code)
	if args.json:
		emit(entry)
	else:
		print_text(entry)
	return 0


def print_text(entry: dict) -> None:
	print(f"recorded {entry['id']} ({entry['type']}) in {NOTEBOOK_PATH}")
	if entry["type"] == "confidence":
		print(f"# judgment on {entry['hypothesis']}")
	if entry["type"] == "observation":
		print(f"# grade: {entry['grade']}")
		supports = entry["evidence"][0].get("supports")
		if supports is not None:
			print(f"# supports: {supports}")
	if "evidence" in entry:
		item = entry["evidence"][0]
		if "job_id" in item:
			template = item["template"]
			named = "no template" if template is None else f"template {template}"
			print(
				f"# evidence: {item['source']} job {item['job_id']} "
				f"{item['state']} ({named}); retrieved {item['retrieved']}; "
				f"grade {item['grade']}"
			)
			artifacts = item.get("artifacts")
			if artifacts is not None:
				counted = f"{len(artifacts['files'])} files"
				total = artifacts.get("total_bytes")
				if total is not None:
					counted += f", {total} bytes"
				print(f"# artifacts: {counted}")
		else:
			print(
				f"# evidence: {item['source']} via {', '.join(item['endpoints'])}; "
				f"retrieved {item['retrieved']}; grade {item['grade']}"
			)
		print(f"# snapshot: {item['snapshot']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
	raise SystemExit(main())
